rationale:
structural: The text requires these structural items: a unit struct `pub struct Css;`, the trait implementations `Clone`, `Debug`, `Default`, `Copy` and `OutlineLang`, and that the `OutlineLang` impl supplies the extension, selection and fingerprint rules. A `Css` type without all of these would violate the text. The macro invocation `language!(Css, css::PROFILE)` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/languages/mod.rs` (root `macro@ace2dde32c5b`) is the root, and it carries the `{impl}` markers. The `language` macro in the same file (`macro[language]`) expands it as follows:
- It declares `pub struct $name;`, which is `pub struct Css;`.
- It adds `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]`.
- It writes `impl super::OutlineLang for $name`. That impl has `name`, `extensions` and `fingerprint_scheme` read from the profile, `outline` via `parse_with`, and `search_structure`.

The invocation passes `css::PROFILE`, which supplies the extension, selection and fingerprint data. The text defers the detail of those rules to the refining declarations in the chapter, which are outside this review. The root covers every structural obligation in the subject text.

behavioral: `requirements.sdk.sources.css.Css` declares the `Css` unit struct and its trait implementations: `Clone`, `Debug`, `Default`, `OutlineLang` and `Copy`. It says `Css` supplies the extension, selection and fingerprint rules described in its chapter. Those rules belong to the refining requirements, such as `requirements.sdk.sources.css.language`, `requirements.sdk.sources.css.fingerprints` and `requirements.sdk.sources.css.items`. They are assessed there, so I did not reassess them here.

The obligations that can be tested here are covered:
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` calls `check(languages::Css, "a.CSS", ".check { color: red; }", "rule[.check]", &["css"], "css-structural-v1")`.
  - Its inner `fn[check]` helper is bounded by `OutlineLang + Default + Copy`, so the test only compiles if `Css` is `Copy`, `Default` and an `OutlineLang`.
  - It asserts that `Css` has size zero, that `Clone::clone` gives a value with the same extensions, and that `L::default().fingerprint_scheme()` is `css-structural-v1`.
  - It asserts the extensions and the fingerprint scheme. It also asserts that `outline()` and `from_source_with` give the same selectors as `from_source`, that an uppercase `.CSS` filename is inferred as CSS, and that `select("rule[.check]")` and `search_structure` work.
  - This establishes that `Css` supplies the extension, selection and fingerprint behavior through `OutlineLang`.
- `fn[css_duplicate_names_are_numbered_after_normalization_within_each_parent]` exercises `Css` selection through the public API. It checks duplicate numbering, per-parent scoping and select results.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` checks that the public export inventory, including `Css`, matches rustdoc.

`Debug` has no direct test. The requirement specifies no Debug output format, and the implementation has no conditional or transformation of its own. I treated that as having no independent observable obligation that needs a test.
